perspective:
**Ethan’s available information:**

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my long-time friend since middle school and works as a doctor.
- I noticed Gary was working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- I invited him to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation/rejuvenation, telling him his health matters and it might give him a new perspective. Gary declined, saying he appreciated it but had too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected there was more to his overworking than professional obligations.
- I confronted Gary, telling him we had been friends since middle school, he could tell me anything, and I was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden me.
- Gary then opened up to me about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- I felt relief and empathy. I offered to help him find better balance, suggesting prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. I saw him making efforts to change; I felt hopeful and proud. Gary told me things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie last weekend. I encouraged him and said I was there whenever he needed to talk.
- After a year, I saw Gary as capable of managing on his own and with a healthier work-life balance. I felt satisfied and happy for him. I decided to step back while telling him I’m always a call away and to keep up the good work. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and felt more in control.
